name: Apple Reminders
description: Apple Reminders is Apple's local and iCloud-backed task application for lists, reminders, completion, due dates, recurrence, priorities, tags, attachments, subtasks, and time- or location-based alerts.
agentUseSummary: Apple Reminders cannot yet be connected through Relay. Apple documents native EventKit access inside an Apple-platform app with explicit per-device full read/write permission, but it publishes no Reminders server API, delegated account scope, client enrollment path, or webhook contract for a Railway-hosted connector; the product must choose and validate a local runtime architecture first.

blocked.label: Connect Apple Reminders
blocked.description: Connect remains unavailable until Relay selects and accepts a supported native runtime and per-device authority model.

blocked.label: Collect Apple credentials
blocked.description: Apple Account passwords, app-specific passwords, verification codes, cookies, session tokens, and private framework material are never collected.

blocked.label: Read reminders
blocked.description: Lists, tasks, titles, notes, URLs, attachments, due dates, locations, priorities, tags, subtasks, recurrence, completion, and collaborators remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Change reminders or use private interfaces
blocked.description: Creating, updating, completing, deleting, moving, or sharing reminders, scraping iCloud.com, private database access, device automation, arbitrary endpoints, and raw responses are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Apple Reminders action is enabled before a supported native runtime architecture and representative acceptance.

runtimeSupport.description: No Apple Reminders wrapper is mounted before the local EventKit runtime and authority architecture is frozen.
No Apple Reminders wrapper is mounted before the local EventKit runtime and authority architecture is frozen.

providerSetup.blocker: Apple's documented Reminders integration surface is EventKit inside an Apple-platform app. It requires explicit per-device full read/write permission even for reads; Apple does not offer read-only Reminders authorization. Apple's iCloud guidance documents Apple-device and signed-in iCloud.com use, while public developer documentation does not publish a Reminders server endpoint, delegated account scope, app enrollment, token lifecycle, webhook, quota, or Railway-compatible authorization contract.
providerSetup.nextAction: The product and security owners should decide whether Relay may introduce a Mac-local EventKit runtime whose reminders authority is necessarily full read/write. If accepted, an exclusive task must build the signed and permission-declared native boundary, run representative consent, verify sources, fields, recurrence, locations, attachments, change notifications, revocation, offline behavior, mutation confirmations, and disconnect denial before any wrapper is exposed.

evidence.supports: Apple requires explicit user permission through a local EKEventStore and states that reminder reads require full access because read-only reminder authorization is unavailable.
Apple's native sample requires NSRemindersFullAccessUsageDescription and full access that can create, fetch, edit, complete, and delete reminders across all of a person's calendars.
Apple documents native reminder creation, editing, completion, saving, and deletion and requires specific user confirmation before an app modifies the Calendar database.
Apple documents iCloud Reminders access through signed-in Apple devices and iCloud.com rather than a third-party developer endpoint.
